newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore February non-oil exports fall 7.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore February non-oil exports fall 7.9 pct.

text.p: Singapore's non-oil domestic exports fell a nominal 7.9 percent year-on-year in February to Singapore $5.52 billion (US$3.86 billion), the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Thursday.
The TDB said the February fall reflected continued sluggish demand for electronics products, especially semiconductors.
Electronics and related industries account for 58 percent of Singapore's domestic exports.
The TDB statement said February non-oil exports fell 4.4 percent in real terms to S$7.12 billion after rising 1.4 percent in January.
On Tuesday, a Reuters poll of 16 economists had forecast am average 1.5 percent rise in the nominal figure.
The forecasts, however, were unusually disparate, ranging from a 5.0 percent drop to a 10 percent rise.
The economists said the wide range reflected general uncertainty about the uptrend in exports after weaker-than-expected January manufacturing growth.
